Subject: RE: SlateOps renewal — commercial counter

Folks — recommending a pragmatic counter to keep the deal moving while protecting unit economics. Proposed commercial summary for customer-facing note: 

- Term: 12 months (start July 1)
- Effective list repricing: hold current rates for 6 months from renewal (price-hold through Dec 31).
- Discount: 7% off list recurring for first 6 months (then revert to standard pricing).
- One-time operational credit: $75,000 applied to first invoice (to offset go-live costs).
- Tiered rebate (6 months):
  * 120-140% of committed units: 15% rebate on incremental consumption
  * 140-160%: 25% rebate on incremental consumption
  * >160%: 40% rebate on incremental consumption
- Invoice terms: first invoice Net 30 (standard), but offer Net 60 only upon signed PO and confirmed procurement timeline (we can accept a separate signed PO to trigger Net 60 for the first invoice).

Rationale: bigger credit (75k) and slightly smaller % discount balances Cost of Goods during bursts. Tiered rebate protects us at extreme tails while giving SlateOps meaningful relief at expected burst levels.

Lauren — can you draft the short redline for an amendment (MSA addendum) and add the DocuSign flow? Monica — ops/implementation confirm any impact to onboarding windows.

Ben
Head of Commercials — Enterprise Renewals
